title: The Hong Kong Handover: Framework and Practice
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
On 1 July 1997, sovereignty over Hong Kong was transferred from the United Kingdom to the People's Republic of China. The event ended British administration and established the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Calling it merely a change of flag would understate the legal transfer; calling it immediate institutional uniformity would also be inaccurate.

The Basic Law created a constitutional framework under the principle commonly described as “one country, two systems.” It states that Hong Kong is an inalienable part of China while providing for a high degree of autonomy and maintaining distinct economic and legal arrangements in specified fields. This design does not mean two sovereign states. It allocates authority inside one sovereign state, reserving some matters to the central authorities and assigning others to regional institutions.

A text, however, does not implement itself. Courts, legislatures, executives, central institutions, civil servants, businesses, and residents interpret and operate the framework. Evaluation must therefore ask separate questions: What does the text say? Which institution has authority to interpret it? What action occurred? What procedure was used? What practical effect followed? Combining these questions into one political label prevents precise disagreement.

The framework's operation has been contested, especially when security, electoral arrangements, public order, and civil liberties intersect. A careful reader should neither assume that every institutional difference proves complete independence nor assume that formal continuity proves unchanged lived conditions. Legal analysis needs sources and jurisdiction; historical analysis needs sequence; social analysis needs evidence about practice. The handover is best understood as a defined transfer followed by an ongoing and disputed process of constitutional operation.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The handover changed only symbols and no legal authority.

options.label: B
options.text: Hong Kong became a second sovereign state in 1997.

options.label: C
options.text: The handover involved a sovereignty transfer, a constitutional allocation of authority, and contested institutional practice.

options.label: D
options.text: Legal texts automatically determine every social outcome.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は主権移転、国家内部の権限配分、その継続的で争われる運用を区別します。Aは法的移転、Bは一国家内の設計、Dは実施主体と効果を無視します。

questions.prompt: Which two simplifications does paragraph 1 reject?

options.label: A
options.text: That only a flag changed, and that all institutions immediately became uniform with those of mainland China

options.label: B
options.text: That sovereignty transferred, and that British administration ended

options.label: C
options.text: That Hong Kong became a special administrative region, and that a Basic Law exists

options.label: D
options.text: That legal and practical analysis require evidence

questions.answer: 正解：A。「旗だけの変更」という過小評価と、「直ちに制度が完全に一様化した」という単純化の両方を退けます。B・Cは本文の事実、Dは分析方針です。

questions.prompt: The phrase “allocate authority” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: divide responsibilities among institutions

options.label: B
options.text: erase all legal distinctions

options.label: C
options.text: measure public opinion only

options.label: D
options.text: transfer every power abroad

questions.answer: 正解：A。一つの主権国家内で中央と地域の制度へ責任・権限を配分する意味です。B～Dは区別の消去、世論測定、国外移転であり異なります。

questions.prompt: Why does “one country, two systems” not mean two sovereign states in this passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The Basic Law identifies Hong Kong as part of China and distributes powers between central and regional institutions within one sovereign state.

options.label: B
options.text: It grants every regional institution complete authority over all matters.

options.label: C
options.text: It removes all distinct economic and legal arrangements.

options.label: D
options.text: It leaves sovereignty with the United Kingdom after 1997.

questions.answer: 正解：A。香港を中国の不可分の一部と位置づけた上で、国家内部の中央・地域間で権限を配分します。B～Dは権限留保、制度差、主権移転に反します。

questions.prompt: What analytical procedure follows from the statement “A text does not implement itself”?

options.label: A
options.text: Examine separately the text, authorized interpreters, actual actions, procedures used, and practical effects.

options.label: B
options.text: Assume the written text automatically produces every claimed social result.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore courts, executives, residents, and other actors operating the framework.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace all specific evidence with a single political label.

questions.answer: 正解：A。法文、解釈権限、実施行為、手続、実際の効果を別々に証拠で確認します。B～Dはまさに本文が避ける自動実施の仮定とラベル化です。

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of separating authority, procedure, and effect in institutional evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: It reveals whether disagreement concerns the existence of power, the way it was exercised, or the outcome, and clarifies the evidence needed.

options.label: B
options.text: It guarantees that every observer will reach the same political conclusion.

options.label: C
options.text: It makes actual outcomes irrelevant whenever formal authority exists.

options.label: D
options.text: It permits analysts to ignore disputed procedures.

questions.answer: 正解：A。権限の有無、行使手続、実際の効果のどこが争点かを特定し、必要な証拠を明確にできます。Bは合意を保証しすぎ、C・Dは重要な分析層を捨てます。

questions.prompt: Why do legal, historical, and social analyses require different kinds of evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: Legal analysis examines norms and jurisdiction, history examines sequence and change, and social analysis examines actual behavior and experience.

options.label: B
options.text: All three disciplines ask only what one constitutional sentence says.

options.label: C
options.text: Historical analysis does not need the order of events.

options.label: D
options.text: Social analysis can infer lived conditions from formal continuity alone.

questions.answer: 正解：A。法学は規範・権限、歴史学は出来事の順序・変化、社会分析は行動・経験を主対象にします。B～Dは各分野の証拠要件を消します。

questions.prompt: What does “Combining these questions into one political label prevents precise disagreement” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: A broad label hides whether the dispute concerns a text, interpretive authority, an action, a procedure, or a practical effect.

options.label: B
options.text: Political labels always identify the exact source and evidence of disagreement.

options.label: C
options.text: Precise disagreement is harmful because it makes claims testable.

options.label: D
options.text: Legal and social questions should never be distinguished.

questions.answer: 正解：A。一括したラベルでは、どの法文・権限・行為・手続・効果に異論があるか特定できません。Aのように分ければ証拠で検討可能です。B～Dは本文の主張と逆です。

questions.prompt: Which evidence framework would best evaluate institutional autonomy?

options.label: A
options.text: Map formal powers and interpreters, build a timeline of decisions and procedures, and measure practical remedies, discretion, and effects on organizations and residents.

options.label: B
options.text: Use one political label without identifying events, institutions, or outcomes.

options.label: C
options.text: Treat every institutional difference as proof of a separate sovereign state.

options.label: D
options.text: Treat formal continuity as proof that lived conditions never changed.

questions.answer: 正解：A。形式的権限と解釈主体、時系列の決定・手続、救済・裁量・生活上の効果という三層で評価します。Bは証拠を曖昧にし、C・Dは本文が戒める両極の推論です。
